0.content: [Nature(Ebenmaß protects its luxury by sorting the unwanted, the low-status and the potentially useful before they disturb the main house); Practice(a dirty peasant, drunk soldier or obvious beggar is intercepted outside or in the service yard, washed if salvageable, fed or dismissed if not, and removed immediately from guest view if likely to offend patrons); Courtesy(low-born members of a wealthy party are accepted according to declared role—servant, guard, clerk, musician or dependent—and housed, bathed or fed through the backstairs system without pretending they are guests); Opportunity(a pretty, educated, talented or unusually composed arrival may be tested discreetly for temporary work or permanent employment); Pressure(class shame, false identities, desperate ambition and patron embarrassment collide whenever someone does not clearly belong where they have arrived); Hook(a noble refuses to acknowledge his own filthy companion, a servant claims gentility, or the house discovers that the person sent to the side door is more valuable than the one who entered through the front).]

1.content: [Nature(after supper the estate divides into smaller rooms for cards, dancing, music, drinking, conversation and private company rather than forcing every guest into one entertainment); Appeal(a shy visitor can find quiet music while a loud party loses money three doors away, making Ebenmaß unusually good at giving people the evening they imagined); Practice(companions circulate according to talent and preference, turning awkward gatherings into lively ones without appearing to manage them); Pressure(wagers, flirtations and performances let guests prove wit, wealth or desirability before people whose opinion suddenly matters); Hook(a harmless wager becomes expensive, somebody dedicates the wrong song, or two guests discover they expected the same companion or private room).]

2.content: [Place(a warm bath wing opens onto a walled pear courtyard, with tiled pools, private tubs, shaving rooms and attendants carrying heated linen); Appeal(after Reikland roads, armour, coaches and cold inns, clean skin, hot water and an afternoon with nowhere urgent to be feels obscenely luxurious); Social(friends bathe together, companions may attend, and private rooms allow quieter conversation away from dining halls); Pressure(people speak differently without uniforms, weapons or servants immediately beside them, exposing scars, illnesses, affairs and anxieties they normally conceal); Hook(a guest recognises an old wound, clothing disappears from the wrong room, or an apparently casual conversation becomes an offer nobody expected to receive).]

3.content: [Name: Sybilla Mersing; Age: 20; Role: courtesan and dancer whose speciality is turning restrained young guests into people who will regret breakfast; Appearance: small striking woman with pale freckled skin, unruly black curls, strong legs and fashionable dresses altered repeatedly for dancing; Daily Life: joins drinking parties, dances, plays dice and cards, entertains guests and sleeps through much of any morning she can defend from household schedules; Habit: wins buttons from guests instead of coins and has accumulated enough silver, horn and enamel fastenings to decorate a small regiment; Wants: become famous enough that visiting nobles ask for her by name before seeing her; Pressure: Sybilla is excellent at making a dull evening memorable and therefore regularly gets blamed for debts, broken furniture and quarrels that were already waiting to happen; Competence: dancing, dice, quick hands and making shy people laugh; Relationships: Valentin is friend and competitive nuisance, Elsbeth repairs her abused clothes and Margarethe has formally forbidden her from entering the wine cellar alone.]

4.content: [Name: Arno Velten; Age: 35; Role: courtesan, fencing partner and riding companion popular with officers, widows and guests who prefer broad shoulders to poetry; Appearance: tall muscular man with cropped brown hair, broken nose set almost straight, old sabre scar across one shoulder and immaculate moustache; Daily Life: fences with guests, rides the estate lanes, entertains privately and spends mornings repairing gloves, belts and worn sword furniture from an abandoned saddler’s apprenticeship; Habit: wagers small coins on almost anything; Wants: purchase a decent horse entirely with gambling winnings, which has prevented him purchasing one with wages for six years; Pressure: young officers regularly turn friendly fencing into attempts to prove something stupid; Competence: fencing, horses, leatherwork and recognising military bluff; Relationships: Jost patches him after bad bouts, Ruprecht occasionally borrows him to calm military guests and Sabine insists he cannot recognise danger when it is wearing a uniform.]

5.content: [Name: Hester Vollmar; Age: 43; Role: established courtesan preferred by older nobles, officers and wealthy patrons who have little interest in pretending they are twenty; Appearance: handsome full-figured woman with dark-blond hair streaked silver, strong nose, excellent teeth and expensive gowns chosen to flatter rather than chase fashion; Daily Life: entertains regulars, joins long dinners, plays cards and quietly teaches younger companions which important men are fools, bores or unexpectedly decent company; Habit: remembers patrons by the first ridiculous thing they boasted about rather than by title; Wants: remain expensive long after younger beauty stops being available as an advantage; Pressure: some men who visited her as young officers now return with grown sons who know considerably less about their fathers than Hester does; Competence: cards, military gossip, family histories and detecting men pretending to possess money; Relationships: Ruprecht values her memory, Margarethe drinks cheap beer with her after closing and Hester thinks Sabine worries too much.]

6.content: [Name: Mirelle Vautrin; Age: 29; Origin: Bretonnia, Parravon; Role: courtesan and dancer known for expensive manners, foreign songs and making provincial nobles feel more sophisticated than they are; Appearance: long auburn hair, narrow amused eyes, dancer’s build and richly fitted gowns combining Bretonnian cuts with Reiklander fashion; Daily Life: receives guests, dances after supper, accompanies private dinners and helps the household judge visiting Bretonnian tastes; Habit: keeps a list of the worst Bretonnian phrases attempted by Reiklanders and performs them back perfectly months later; Wants: enough money to eventually open a fashionable dancing house rather than another brothel; Pressure: patrons pay for exaggerated Bretonnian romance while becoming offended when Mirelle laughs at their ideas of Bretonnia; Competence: dancing, manners, accents and reading status from clothing; Relationships: Sabine trusts her with difficult noble parties, while Valentin considers every Bretonnian song an invitation to musical warfare.]

7.content: [Name: Elsbeth Krumholz; Age: 20; Role: laundry hand and improving seamstress responsible for guest linen and clothing repairs; Appearance: freckled short-haired young woman in a plain apron with needles pinned safely inside one cuff; Daily Life: boils sheets, removes stains, patches torn clothes and carries finished linen between wings; Habit: cuts monograms from linen too ruined to save and stitches them inside her work apron, saying great names may as well do some washing; Wants: promotion to full seamstress before her hands are permanently spoiled by lye; Pressure: her family accepts her wages while telling neighbours she works as a respectable lady’s maid; Past: left a noble household where servants were struck for mistakes and considers Ebenmaß’s emotional coldness preferable; Competence: sewing, stains and identifying expensive cloth; Relationships: Sabine pays for delicate repairs and Valentin is her favourite recurring disaster; Speech: quiet until somebody mistakes invisibility for stupidity.]

8.content: [Name: Jost Achenbach; Age: 41; Role: bathmaster and barber-surgeon tending guests and household staff; Appearance: burly close-shaven man with heavy moustache, scarred hands and an apron that rarely stays clean; Daily Life: supervises hot baths, shaves guests, pulls teeth, stitches cuts, sets minor injuries and treats common pox or skin complaints before referring serious illness onward; Habit: keeps extracted teeth in labelled paper packets until the bill is settled because titled patients have accused him of removing the wrong one afterward; Wants: people to become sober before asking him to use sharp instruments; Pressure: discretion means he sees injuries, diseases and bruises patrons desperately want attributed to something respectable; Competence: practical surgery, bathing, drunken injuries and knowing when not to operate; Relationships: Sabine sends worried workers to him and Elsbeth despises what he does to clean linen.]

9.content: [Name: Valentin Saffran; Age: 23; Role: lutenist, singer and companion popular with younger guests; Appearance: slender curly-haired man in embroidered second-hand finery, with one pierced ear and a lute maintained better than his boots; Daily Life: plays during meals, takes private company when desired and learns new songs from travellers; Habit: turns guests’ boasts into comic verses under false names, then forgets to disguise them sufficiently; Wants: recognition as a musician beyond Ebenmaß without surrendering the money and freedom the house gives him; Pressure: admirers offer patronage that sounds increasingly like ownership, while respectable musicians dismiss where he works; Competence: music, mimicry, flirting and improvisation; Weakness: catastrophically poor at saving money; Relationships: Sabine considers him talented and reckless, while Elsbeth repairs clothing he repeatedly tears showing off.]

10.content: [Name: Sabine Ketterling; Age: 34; Role: senior companion who receives regular patrons and helps younger companions judge difficult guests; Appearance: dark-curled elegant woman in fashionable but practical evening dress, usually carrying a small commonplace book; Daily Life: entertains, reads with guests, negotiates private arrangements and advises companions after unpleasant encounters; Habit: records good jokes, terrible poetry and useful lies in the same book without identifying which is which; Wants: enough money and standing to choose fewer clients without becoming somebody’s kept possession; Pressure: wealthy regulars increasingly confuse long familiarity with rights over her time; Competence: etiquette, conversation, seduction and recognising insecurity beneath arrogance; Relationships: trusts Ruprecht to enforce refusals, needles Valentin about his judgement and pays Elsbeth extra for invisible repairs; Limit: affection may be genuine, entitlement never becomes romance.]

11.content: [Name: Ruprecht Vellner; Age: 52; Role: house steward responsible for rooms, staff assignments, guest conduct and the Red Bell; Appearance: tall narrow man with iron-grey hair, immaculate black wool and two crooked fingers from an old break; Daily Life: receives important guests, settles complaints, checks staffing and personally attends serious Red Bells; Habit: uses a troublesome noble’s complete title while having him removed; Wants: Ebenmaß profitable enough that its rules remain stronger than any single patron; Pressure: servants expect protection while powerful guests expect exceptions; Competence: rank, household management, de-escalation and remembering previous misconduct; Relationships: trusts Sabine’s account of private incidents and fights Margarethe continually over cellar expenditure; Limit: violence against staff ends hospitality regardless of pedigree; Speech: formal, dry and more courteous as his patience worsens.]

12.content: [Custom(twice weekly vintners, cheesemakers, bakers, poulterers and growers bring selected goods to Ebenmaß for tasting and purchase); Status(a regular house contract pays well and advertises a producer to wealthy guests, making acceptance valuable beyond the immediate sale); Practice(the buyers judge quality rather than lineage, so small producers occasionally embarrass prestigious estates); Pressure(poor harvests, bribery, adulterated lots and patrons demanding constant novelty can threaten livelihoods outside the house); Social(rejected food is often still excellent and may be sold cheaply to employees or neighbouring households); Hook(a famous wine forgery, an unknown dairy suddenly produces exceptional cheese, or a family risks ruin after losing its contract).]

13.content: [Term(workers call the flat quiet following long periods of anticipating, flattering and performing pleasure for other people the 'Hush'); Expression(off-duty staff often prefer plain food, silence, practical conversation and being left physically alone, with flirtation among employees treated as genuine only when clearly invited); Reality(many previously endured beatings, coercion, withheld wages or sexual harassment elsewhere and consider emotional dullness preferable to fear); Pressure(safe pay and enforceable boundaries make leaving difficult even for workers who worry that little outside the house still excites them); Knowledge(staff generally explain the Hush as exhaustion from service work); Preserve(no supernatural cause is established here, and sex work itself is not treated as degrading).]

14.content: [Custom(each evening Ebenmaß serves a long informal supper before private entertainments, with companions and musicians mixing among guests rather than waiting invisibly for summons); Social(rank remains visible but seating, drinking and conversation cross boundaries unusual in respectable noble houses); Practice(attending supper purchases food and company, not sexual access to anyone afterward); Pressure(flirtation, business, jealousy, wagers and accidental recognition develop easily when people expected to remain discreet share the same table); Reputation(many regulars insist the supper is the best part while spending considerably more after it).]
